findings.description: The provider count saved in _walk_estimate is not reused by the walk-loop input gate, which recalculates estimate_tokens(messages).
findings.failure_mode: If the heuristic exceeds 180K but count_tokens returns less than 180K, preflight accepts the request and the walk loop subsequently rejects it as ROUTING_MISS. A valid request can exhaust the chain without being dispatched.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the authoritative _walk_estimate consistently for subsequent input checks instead of recalculating the heuristic.

findings.description: The context-limit handler continues the bounded retry loop after shrinking max_tokens, even when no iteration remains.
findings.failure_mode: With max_retries=0, or a context error on the final attempt, the smaller request is never sent. Execution falls through to RetriesExhaustedError, losing the provider context verdict and bypassing cheval's calibration record and non-walkable exit.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly allocate the single shrink attempt, or re-raise the original ProviderContextLimitError when no retry remains.

findings.description: _ceiling_unverified describes only the head entry but controls context-limit classification and rate-limit handling for every fallback.
findings.failure_mode: After an unverified head fails, a calibrated fallback's rate limit incorrectly terminates the chain as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED. Conversely, an unverified fallback following a verified head misses the required calibration handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute verification status from each current hop's policy bound, calibration, and input count before dispatch, and use that status in both exception handlers.

findings.description: Every RateLimitError while unverified triggers calibration and an immediate exit, including ordinary request-rate limits.
findings.failure_mode: A requests-per-minute 429 above the probed bound prevents fallback dispatch even though it provides no evidence that the payload exceeds a token limit. The supplied test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop exercises this failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the error's token_limited classification before taking the calibration exit; retain normal chain walking for request-rate limits.

findings.description: Long-context eligibility checks only input_tokens, although Anthropic cache-read and cache-creation tokens are supplied separately and are part of the request's input.
findings.failure_mode: A request containing 1K uncached tokens and 250K cached tokens stays below the 200K threshold in this calculation. Its input, cache, and output charges omit the premium, underreporting ledger costs and budget consumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the threshold against input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens, then apply the premium to all applicable cost components.

findings.description: The pre-flight now replaces the heuristic estimate with the provider's count_tokens value (`_preflight_estimated = _preflight_outcome.estimate.tokens`, `_walk_estimate = _preflight_estimated`, lines 1841-1842) and dispatches on it. The per-hop walk gate immediately below the new `_lookup_max_input_tokens(..., max_tokens=_hop_budget)` call still re-imports and runs the raw `estimate_tokens(messages)` heuristic against the same policy bound. The two gates now evaluate different numbers against the same threshold.
findings.failure_mode: Default `probed` policy, bound 180K: a prompt whose heuristic is 185K but whose provider count is 175K passes the pre-flight (count is authoritative near the bound), then every hop in the chain is skipped as ROUTING_MISS by the heuristic gate, and the call exits CHAIN_EXHAUSTED with no dispatch. The count endpoint makes the outcome strictly worse than before the change, and the envelope shows `preflight_decision: dispatch/warn` next to an all-miss walk.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `_walk_estimate` (falling back to `estimate_tokens(messages)` only when it is None) in the per-hop gate comparison, mirroring what the I1 fit block already does at lines 2087-2090.

findings.description: The one-shot output-budget shrink does `request = replace(request, max_tokens=room); continue` without setting `last_typed_error = e` and without checking whether this is the final iteration of `for attempt in range(max_retries + 1)`. When the ProviderContextLimitError arrives on the last attempt (earlier attempts consumed by 429/503 backoff, or `max_retries == 0`), the loop simply ends and the post-loop RetriesExhaustedError is raised with no typed context.
findings.failure_mode: cheval's `except ProviderContextLimitError` arm never fires; the RetriesExhaustedError is handled by the generic walk path, so the same oversized payload is sent to the next voice (exactly what D-1.1b says must not happen), no `.run/ceiling-observed.json` row is written, and the operator never sees `calibration_needed`. With `max_retries=0` the shrink retry never executes at all and the error is silently downgraded.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `last_typed_error = e` in the arm; if `attempt == max_retries` (or the global attempt budget is exhausted) re-raise `e` instead of `continue`. Alternatively perform the single shrink retry outside the attempt budget so it is always attempted exactly once.

findings.description: `_ceiling_unverified` is assigned once from the head entry's GateOutcome (line 1843) and then consulted inside the per-hop loop on every hop's `except RateLimitError` (line 2296) and `except ProviderContextLimitError` (line 2256). A fallback hop has its own catalog entry, probed bound and calibration state, but inherits the head's verdict. Additionally, the 429 arm short-circuits on any RateLimitError, with no distinction between a token-limit 429 and a plain requests-per-minute 429, although the comment and the D-1.1b design describe the token-limit class only.
findings.failure_mode: Under `LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived`, the head fails walkably (503), the chain walks to a calibrated fallback that is well within its verified bound, the fallback returns an ordinary RPM 429, and the invocation ends with exit RATE_LIMITED and a spurious `RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED` calibration row for the fallback model instead of walking to the next hop. A provider context verdict on the calibrated fallback is also mislabeled CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute an unverified flag per hop (e.g. from `_ceiling_input_bound` for `_entry` versus `_walk_estimate`, or `_idx == 0 and _preflight_outcome.unverified`) and use it in both arms; gate the 429 short-circuit on the token-limit class (e.g. a `token_limited` attribute on RateLimitError) so request-rate 429s keep walking.

findings.cross_file_justification: The zero is written by the diff-touched closure in cheval.py; readers of the store (`routing/ceiling.py::observed_for`, `scripts/loa-status.sh::_anthropic_ceiling_json`) are also in this PR but were truncated from the view. The primary reviewer reports loa-status.sh prints `observed -1` for such a row while the Python reducer skips it.
findings.description: `_obs = int(observed) if observed > 0 else int(_walk_estimate or 0)`: when the gate is disabled (`LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_INPUT_GATE=1`) and the provider's message carries no parsable numbers, `_walk_estimate` is None and a row with `observed_input_tokens: 0` is appended to the store unconditionally.
findings.failure_mode: A meaningless 0 row persists in `.run/ceiling-observed.json`; any reader that does not filter non-positive values derives a bound of -1 (status output) and the two readers disagree about the model's ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip `_ceiling_record_observed` (but keep the typed exit and envelope) when `_obs <= 0`, or compute the estimate on demand with `estimate_tokens(messages)` before recording.

findings.description: The long-context premium triggers on `input_tokens > threshold` only. Per the ledger docstring, Anthropic's `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens` are not part of `input_tokens`, yet the provider's published 1M-window rule applies the premium when the total prompt (uncached + cached) exceeds 200K. The function then multiplies `cr_cost` and `cw_cost` by the input multiplier, so it knows cache traffic is input-side, but excludes it from the threshold test.
findings.failure_mode: A cache-heavy request (e.g. 150K uncached + 100K cache_read) is billed at standard rates in the ledger while the provider bills the premium; `long_context` is not set on the row and cost-report.sh undercounts spend for exactly the workloads most likely to exceed 200K.
findings.suggested_fix: Test the threshold against `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens`, and document the chosen basis next to the `verified: False` catalog flag.

findings.cross_file_justification: `_ceiling_record_observed` is invoked from this diff-touched closure; the primary reviewer reports `routing/ceiling.py::record_observed` (in the PR, truncated here) performs an unlocked read-modify-write of the JSON store. The same repo guards the cost ledger and daily-spend sidecar with `fcntl.flock` + `O_NOFOLLOW` (`metering/ledger.py::append_ledger`, `update_daily_spend`).
findings.description: Flatline runs several cheval processes in parallel; two voices hitting the provider limit at once each read the store, append their row, and rewrite the file. Without a lock the second writer drops the first's observation. The record path also lacks the symlink/regular-file checks the other `.run/` writers apply to env-redirectable paths.
findings.failure_mode: Lost observed-bound rows mean the next call is not bounded by an observation that was actually made, re-sending a payload the provider has already rejected; a planted symlink at `LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH` would be followed on write.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the ledger pattern: open with `O_NOFOLLOW`, take `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` around read-modify-write (or append JSONL rows instead of rewriting a JSON document), and reject non-regular targets.

findings.description: The provider's raw error body (`str(_exc)`) is interpolated into both the `models_failed[].message_redacted` row and the stderr `_error_json` message. The field name promises redaction, but nothing in this closure applies it; the stderr print in particular bypasses the modelinv emit-time redaction that protects the envelope.
findings.failure_mode: If a provider 400/413 body echoes request content (which can include a secret-shaped fragment from the prompt), it lands verbatim in the operator's stderr log, and in the envelope row if emit-time redaction is ever disabled or patched.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the message through the existing redaction helper before building `_calib`, the `models_failed` row and the `_error_json` text, matching how the other walk-arm rows are produced.
